prompt: In a Capacitor app, what draws the planner's buttons on the phone's screen?

choices.text: Native Android and iOS controls, generated from the HTML
choices.why: Nothing generates native controls from HTML. That is the conversion the lesson says does not exist.

choices.text: A WebView inside the app
choices.why: Right. The app's whole screen is a WebView loading your built site.

choices.text: React Native's views
choices.why: React Native is the other path, and needs the screens written again.

choices.text: A copy of Chrome installed beside the app
choices.why: The WebView is part of the system and embedded in the app; no browser is installed beside it.

prompt: Why can lesson 7 reuse src/planner.ts in a React Native app, but not src/view.ts?

choices.text: React Native cannot run TypeScript
choices.why: It runs TypeScript; the lesson writes its components in it.

choices.text: view.ts uses Vite features that only work in a browser
choices.why: Vite is not the obstacle. The DOM is.

choices.text: view.ts draws with the DOM, and there is no document there
choices.why: Right. planner.ts has no DOM in it; view.ts is nothing but DOM calls.

choices.text: planner.ts is smaller
choices.why: Size has nothing to do with it.

prompt: A team's web app works well, and they want it in the stores within a month without rewriting screens. Which path does the lesson point them to?

choices.text: Wrap it and check its limits
choices.why: Right. The wrapper keeps everything they wrote, and lesson 6 is the check.

choices.text: React Native, because it reuses the HTML
choices.why: React Native reuses logic, not HTML or views.

choices.text: Swift and Kotlin, one app per platform
choices.why: That is a rewrite of everything, twice.

choices.text: A converter that outputs a native project from dist/
choices.why: No such converter exists, which is the lesson's first point.

prompt: Which parts of the course need a Mac? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Apple's signing in lesson 14

choices.text: Electron and Tauri in lessons 11 and 12

choices.text: the Android half of lesson 3

prompt: A student has no Mac. What does the lesson say about lessons 3 and 14?

choices.text: Skip them; nothing in them applies

choices.text: Install Xcode on Linux through a compatibility layer such as Wine, then carry on

choices.text: Read iOS, practise Android
choices.why: Right. The ideas are the same; only the tools differ.

choices.text: Wait for lesson 16
choices.why: Lesson 16 does not replace them.

choices.why: A Gradle build prints plenty; none was run here.

choices.text: The store forbids showing it

prompt: Which path to a working computer does the lesson recommend?

choices.text: A virtual machine running Ubuntu Server, apart from your system
choices.why: A server has no desktop, and lessons 11 and 12 open windows; the VM path names Ubuntu Desktop.

choices.text: Installed on your own computer
choices.why: Right. Windows and phones are easiest where the screen and the USB port are.

choices.text: GitHub Codespaces
choices.why: It has no window and no emulator.

choices.text: A computer the platform lends you
choices.why: The platform provides no machine.

prompt: In a virtual machine, which part of the course is the weak point, according to the lesson?

choices.text: Installing Node.js
choices.why: Node installs the same way inside a VM.

choices.text: Building the planner with Vite
choices.why: Vite runs fine there.

choices.text: The Android emulator
choices.why: Right. It is a virtual machine itself, and runs slowly or not at all inside another one.

choices.text: Git
choices.why: Git does not care.

prompt: node --version prints v18.19.1. What does the lesson tell you to do?

choices.text: Install Node 22 from the system packages as well, and keep both
choices.why: Two copies mean the version depends on which one the terminal finds first.

choices.text: Carry on; any version works
choices.why: The course was recorded on 22, and below 22 is the wrong Node.

choices.text: Install 22.22.0 as lesson 1 of javascript does, once
choices.why: Right. This course uses exactly that installation.

choices.text: Downgrade npm
choices.why: npm is not the problem.

prompt: What does -E change in npm install -E -D vite@8.3.5?

choices.text: package.json records 8.3.5, not ^8.3.5
choices.why: Right. Exact versions, so the same project installs the same files next month.

choices.text: It installs the package globally
choices.why: That is -g.

choices.text: It skips the lockfile so installs are faster
choices.why: The lockfile is still written, and it belongs in git.

choices.text: It marks the package as a development dependency
choices.why: That is -D.

prompt: Why does the lesson say npm run build comes first whenever something looks wrong?

choices.text: It installs every dependency again from the lockfile, which fixes most problems
choices.why: It installs nothing; it checks types and writes dist/.

choices.text: Everything later wraps dist/
choices.why: Right. Every later lesson wraps dist/, and a failed build leaves the old one there.

choices.text: It starts the dev server
choices.why: That is npm run dev.

choices.text: It uploads the app
choices.why: It uploads nothing.

prompt: Vite copies the files in the ___ folder into the built site as they are.
Why do this course's transcripts show the accessibility tree instead of a screenshot?

choices.text: Screenshots are forbidden by Playwright's licence
choices.why: Playwright takes screenshots; the licence is not the reason.

choices.text: The tree loads faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: A screen reader can only read terminals
choices.why: Not the reason, and not true.

choices.text: It can be pasted, and shows what a screen reader is given
choices.why: Right. And a control missing from it is one a screen-reader user cannot find.

prompt: After the second look.mjs run added 25 minutes on 23 October, how many minutes did the week hold?
You add a session in the browser and reload the page. What happens, and why?

choices.text: It is gone: the plan only lives in memory
choices.why: Right. Nothing saves it yet; lesson 4 does.

choices.text: It stays, because Vite writes it to courses.json
choices.why: Vite serves the file; it writes nothing back to it.

choices.text: It stays, because the browser keeps the last DOM
choices.why: A reload builds the DOM from scratch.

choices.text: The page refuses to reload until it is saved
choices.why: Nothing in the planner does that.

prompt: A button drawn with a div and a click listener works with the mouse. What would look.mjs's output show?

choices.text: A button with its text, like the others, because a click listener is what makes a button
choices.why: The tree reports roles, and a div has none of a button's.

choices.text: Its text, but no button
choices.why: Right. A screen reader is not told it can be pressed: the tree is a check on your own app.

choices.text: An error
choices.why: Nothing errors; the control is just missing as a control.

choices.text: Nothing at all, since divs are hidden
choices.why: Its text would still be there.

choices.text: An empty page

prompt: A colleague says Tauri apps are smaller than Electron apps because Tauri compresses Chromium better. What does the lesson's description suggest instead?

choices.text: Tauri apps are not smaller
choices.why: The lesson does not say that; lesson 12 measures it.

choices.text: Tauri strips the DOM out of the app
choices.why: The app still runs in a WebView with a DOM.

choices.text: Tauri carries no Chromium: it uses the WebView the system has
choices.why: Right. Electron carries its own copy into every app; Tauri carries none.

choices.text: Tauri rewrites the app in Rust
choices.why: Only its core is Rust; your app stays web.

prompt: Where does the lockfile belong, and node_modules?

choices.text: Both in git
choices.why: node_modules is rebuilt from the lockfile.

choices.text: The lockfile in git, node_modules not
choices.why: Right. The lockfile is what lets two people install the same files.

choices.text: Neither in git
choices.why: Without the lockfile, installs drift.

choices.text: node_modules in git, the lockfile not
choices.why: The other way round.
